data.name: Charred Shishito Peppers
data.description: Blistered shishitos with flaky salt, lime and a smoked paprika aioli for dipping.
data.sellingLine: A bowl to share while you decide: smoky, salty, and about one in ten has a little kick.
talkingPoints: They go on the grill over high heat until the skins blister.
Most are mild; roughly one in ten is hot, and there’s no telling which.
The aioli is made in house with smoked paprika.
data.say: “A bowl to share while you decide: smoky, salty, and about one in ten has a little kick.”
data.inspiration: The grill is the first thing lit every day, and this was the first snack the kitchen put on it.

steps.title: Toss
steps.detail: Toss peppers in oil and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Grill
steps.detail: Grill over high heat, turning, until blistered all over.

steps.title: Season
steps.detail: Finish with flaky salt and a squeeze of lime.

steps.title: Plate
steps.detail: Pile in a bowl with aioli on the side.

data.name: Smoked Salmon Toast
data.description: House-cured smoked salmon over whipped crème fraîche on toasted rye, with capers, chives and lemon.
data.sellingLine: Silky smoked salmon on toasted rye with whipped crème fraîche. Light, salty and bright.
talkingPoints: The salmon is cured in salt and brown sugar for two days, then cold-smoked.
Crème fraîche is whipped with lemon zest so it stays light.
Capers and chives go on last, so they stay bright.
data.say: “Silky smoked salmon on toasted rye with whipped crème fraîche. Light, salty and bright.”
data.inspiration: A nod to the smoked fish counters at old delis, made into a two-bite toast.
sellingPoints: Great with a glass of white

steps.title: Toast
steps.detail: Toast the rye until crisp at the edges.

steps.title: Spread
steps.detail: Spread crème fraîche edge to edge.

steps.title: Drape
steps.detail: Drape the salmon in loose folds.

steps.title: Finish
steps.detail: Capers, chives, lemon zest and black pepper.

data.name: Crispy Brussels Sprouts
data.description: Flash-fried Brussels sprouts with bacon lardons, red onion and a maple-chili glaze.
data.sellingLine: Crispy on the outside, sweet and a little spicy from the maple-chili glaze.
talkingPoints: They’re halved and flash-fried so the outer leaves go crisp.
The glaze is maple, chili and a splash of soy.
The bacon can come off for a guest who doesn’t eat pork.
data.say: “Crispy on the outside, sweet and a little spicy from the maple-chili glaze.”
data.inspiration: Built for guests who say they don’t like Brussels sprouts.
sellingPoints: Sweet, salty and a little heat

steps.title: Fry
steps.detail: Fry halved sprouts at 350°F until the edges brown.

steps.title: Drain
steps.detail: Drain well and season with salt.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.detail: Toss in a warm bowl with the glaze.

steps.title: Finish
steps.detail: Fold in the warm bacon and serve right away.

data.name: Beef Tartare
data.description: Hand-cut beef with shallot, capers and Dijon, a cured egg yolk and grilled sourdough.
data.sellingLine: Hand-cut to order, bright with capers and mustard, with a rich cured yolk on top.
talkingPoints: The beef is cut by hand to order, never ground.
The egg yolk is cured in salt and sugar for three days, then grated over.
Raw beef and egg: mention the consumer advisory if a guest asks.
data.say: “Hand-cut to order, bright with capers and mustard, with a rich cured yolk on top.”
data.inspiration: A bistro classic, made the way the chef learned it in a small kitchen in Lyon.

steps.title: Cut
steps.detail: Dice the beef by hand into small, even cubes.

steps.title: Dress
steps.detail: Fold in shallot, capers, Dijon and dressing over ice.

steps.title: Shape
steps.detail: Press into a ring on a chilled plate.

steps.title: Finish
steps.detail: Grate the yolk over and add the grilled bread.

data.name: Roasted Beet & Citrus Salad
data.description: Roasted red and gold beets, orange and grapefruit, whipped goat cheese and pistachio.
data.sellingLine: Earthy roasted beets with bright citrus and a cool swipe of whipped goat cheese.
talkingPoints: The beets roast in salt for an hour, then they’re peeled warm.
Citrus is cut into segments to order so it stays juicy.
Pistachio can come off for a nut allergy; the goat cheese can’t be swapped.
data.say: “Earthy roasted beets with bright citrus and a cool swipe of whipped goat cheese.”
data.inspiration: A winter salad: beets from the cellar and citrus at its best.

steps.title: Swipe
steps.detail: Spread the goat cheese across the plate.

steps.title: Build
steps.detail: Arrange beets and citrus over it, alternating colours.

steps.title: Dress
steps.detail: Spoon over the citrus vinaigrette.

steps.title: Finish
steps.detail: Top with pistachio and herbs.

data.name: Apple & Celery Root Salad
data.description: Crisp apple and celery root cut into matchsticks, with greens, parmesan, toasted walnuts and a cider vinaigrette.
data.sellingLine: Light and crunchy: crisp apple and celery root with parmesan and a cider dressing.
talkingPoints: Apple and celery root are cut to order so nothing goes brown.
Celery root tastes like a mild, nutty celery.
Walnuts can come off for a nut allergy.
data.say: “Light and crunchy: crisp apple and celery root with parmesan and a cider dressing.”
data.inspiration: The salad the kitchen eats at family meal, cleaned up for the menu.

steps.title: Cut
steps.detail: Cut apple and celery root into thin matchsticks.

steps.title: Dress
steps.detail: Toss with the vinaigrette and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Pile
steps.detail: Pile high in a chilled bowl.

steps.title: Finish
steps.detail: Top with parmesan and walnuts.

data.name: Wood-Grilled Half Chicken
data.description: A brined half chicken over the wood grill with salsa verde, charred lemon and crispy potatoes.
data.sellingLine: Our signature: brined overnight, cooked over the wood fire, with a bright green salsa verde.
talkingPoints: The chicken is brined for 24 hours, so it stays juicy.
It cooks over oak on the grill for the smoky skin.
It takes about 20 minutes; let the table know when they order.
data.say: “Our signature: brined overnight, cooked over the wood fire, with a bright green salsa verde.”
data.inspiration: The dish the restaurant was built around: one fire, one great chicken.

steps.title: Grill
steps.detail: Grill skin side down over the oak, then turn.

steps.title: Crisp
steps.detail: Smash and fry the fingerlings until golden.

steps.title: Rest
steps.detail: Rest the chicken, then cut through the joints.

steps.title: Plate
steps.detail: Chicken over potatoes, salsa verde and lemon.

plating.name: Chicken
plating.note: leaning on the potatoes, skin up

data.name: Seared Scallops
data.description: Dry-packed sea scallops seared hard, with roasted cauliflower, brown butter and pickled shallot.
data.sellingLine: Sea scallops with a deep golden crust, roasted cauliflower and nutty brown butter.
talkingPoints: Dry-packed scallops, so they take a real sear.
The cauliflower is roasted hard until the edges are nutty.
Shellfish: always confirm allergies before you fire it.
data.say: “Sea scallops with a deep golden crust, roasted cauliflower and nutty brown butter.”
data.inspiration: Brown butter, cauliflower and scallops: three sweet, nutty things on one plate.

steps.title: Dry
steps.detail: Pat the scallops dry and season just before searing.

steps.title: Sear
steps.detail: Sear in a smoking pan without moving them.

steps.title: Baste
steps.detail: Flip, add butter and baste.

steps.title: Plate
steps.detail: Cauliflower first, scallops on top, brown butter over.

plating.name: Scallops
plating.note: four in a row, crust up

data.name: Braised Lamb Shank
data.description: Lamb shank braised in red wine until it falls from the bone, over creamy polenta with gremolata.
data.sellingLine: Slow-braised in red wine for hours; it comes off the bone with a spoon.
talkingPoints: It braises for about four hours in red wine and stock.
The gremolata (lemon, parsley, garlic) brightens it up.
A big plate: good for a hungry guest or a cold night.
data.say: “Slow-braised in red wine for hours; it comes off the bone with a spoon.”
data.inspiration: A cold-weather dish, cooked low and slow while the dining room sets up.

steps.title: Heat
steps.detail: Warm the shank in its braise in the oven.

steps.title: Polenta
steps.detail: Loosen polenta with stock and parmesan.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.detail: Spoon reduced sauce over the shank.

steps.title: Plate
steps.detail: Polenta, shank upright, gremolata on top.

data.name: Hanger Steak Frites
data.description: Grilled hanger steak sliced against the grain with chimichurri and hand-cut fries.
data.sellingLine: A big-flavoured steak cooked over the grill, with fresh chimichurri and our hand-cut fries.
talkingPoints: Hanger is the butcher’s cut: rich and beefy. We suggest medium-rare.
Fries are cut by hand and cooked twice.
Chimichurri is parsley, oregano, garlic, chili and vinegar.
data.say: “A big-flavoured steak cooked over the grill, with fresh chimichurri and our hand-cut fries.”
data.inspiration: Steak frites, with Argentina’s chimichurri in place of the usual butter.

steps.title: Grill
steps.detail: Grill to temp, turning once.

steps.title: Fry
steps.detail: Fry the blanched fries at 375°F until golden.

steps.title: Rest
steps.detail: Rest the steak, then slice against the grain.

steps.title: Plate
steps.detail: Steak fanned, fries beside, chimichurri over.

data.name: Wild Mushroom Risotto
data.description: Carnaroli risotto with roasted wild mushrooms, thyme, parmesan and a little truffle butter.
data.sellingLine: Creamy, made to order, with a pile of roasted wild mushrooms and a little truffle butter.
talkingPoints: Made to order: it takes about 18 minutes.
The mushrooms change with what the forager brings in.
Vegetarian; we use vegetable stock.
data.say: “Creamy, made to order, with a pile of roasted wild mushrooms and a little truffle butter.”
data.inspiration: The vegetarian main the kitchen is proudest of.

steps.title: Finish
steps.detail: Finish the risotto with hot stock, stirring.

steps.title: Mount
steps.detail: Off the heat, beat in parmesan and butter.

steps.title: Roast
steps.detail: Flash the mushrooms in a hot pan with thyme.

steps.title: Plate
steps.detail: Risotto spread flat, mushrooms on top.

data.name: Wrenfield Burger
data.description: Two smashed patties, aged cheddar, onion jam and house pickles on a toasted brioche bun, with fries.
data.sellingLine: Two crispy smashed patties, sharp cheddar and sweet onion jam. The one regulars order.
talkingPoints: The patties are smashed thin on the flat-top for crispy edges.
Onion jam cooks low for two hours.
Can go in a lettuce wrap; the bun has egg and dairy.
data.say: “Two crispy smashed patties, sharp cheddar and sweet onion jam. The one regulars order.”
data.inspiration: The staff vote for best family meal, put on the menu.

steps.title: Smash
steps.detail: Smash the beef thin on a very hot flat-top.

steps.title: Cheese
steps.detail: Flip, add cheddar, stack the patties.

steps.title: Build
steps.detail: Bun, pickles, patties, onion jam, top bun.

steps.title: Plate
steps.detail: Burger cut in half, fries beside.

data.name: Grilled Pound Cake
data.description: Brown butter pound cake, grilled until crisp at the edges, with whipped cream and macerated berries.
data.sellingLine: Warm pound cake straight off the grill, with cold whipped cream and sweet berries.
talkingPoints: Baked each afternoon, then grilled to order.
The butter is browned first, so the cake tastes nutty (there are no nuts in it).
Big enough for two to share.
data.say: “Warm pound cake straight off the grill, with cold whipped cream and sweet berries.”
data.inspiration: The grill is still warm at the end of the night, so dessert goes on it too.
sellingPoints: No nuts, despite the nutty taste

steps.title: Butter
steps.detail: Brush the slices with melted butter.

steps.title: Grill
steps.detail: Grill until marked and crisp at the edges.

steps.title: Plate
steps.detail: Overlap the slices; spoon berries over.

steps.title: Finish
steps.detail: Whipped cream and a drizzle of honey.

data.name: Chocolate Pot de Crème
data.description: Dark chocolate custard with whipped crème fraîche and a cocoa nib tuile.
data.sellingLine: Silky dark chocolate custard, not too sweet, with a little cream on top.
talkingPoints: A baked custard: rich but small.
The crème fraîche keeps it from tasting too sweet.
The tuile has gluten; it can come off.
data.say: “Silky dark chocolate custard, not too sweet, with a little cream on top.”
data.inspiration: The French classic, served in a small jar so it fits after a big dinner.

steps.title: Temper
steps.detail: Pull the jar 5 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Top
steps.detail: Pipe crème fraîche on top.

steps.title: Dust
steps.detail: Dust lightly with cocoa.

steps.title: Finish
steps.detail: Stand the tuile in the cream.

plating.name: Jar
plating.note: on a small plate with a spoon
